# agave: GPU runs from this repo

`agave run <script> --on kaggle|colab` puts one script from this repo on a GPU, runs it, and brings back the
folder the script wrote to. Everything else (VM, clone, pip install, cleanup, timeout) is agave's job.

## The contract with a script

- Write every result into the directory named by the `OUTPUT_DIR` environment variable. Only that folder comes
  back. `OUTPUT_DIR = os.environ.get("OUTPUT_DIR", "outputs")` keeps local runs working.
- Fail loudly: a non-zero exit is reported as `FAILED` with the log; a swallowed exception is invisible.
- Print what matters (GPU name, dtype, timings). Kaggle logs are only readable after the run ends.
- Dependencies go in the file named by `requirements` in `agave.toml` (normally `requirements.txt`).

## The loop

```
git add -A && git commit -m "..." && git push      # what runs is what is on GitHub; agave refuses otherwise
agave run experiments/my_idea.py --on kaggle       # or --on colab [--gpu T4|L4|G4|A100|H100]
agave outputs                                      # files that came back (outputs/latest/ is the newest run)
agave logs                                         # its log, noise filtered; --full for everything
```

Rules that agave enforces, so do not fight them:
- `--on` is required; there is no default backend. Kaggle is free (30 h/week, T4 only, ~2 min overhead, no live
  log). Colab costs compute units, streams live, and has L4/A100/H100. `--gpu` defaults to T4, the cheapest.
- A dirty or unpushed tree is refused. Commit and push first.
- Every run has a hard timeout, default 1200 s (`--timeout`). A script that needs longer must say so.
- A script whose exact bytes already ran is refused; `--override` runs it anyway. Any edit is a new script.
- One Kaggle run at a time. `agave status` shows what is open; `agave wait` collects a `--no-wait` run.

## Stopping a run

- Ctrl-C on a Colab run stops the VM. `agave kill` stops the most recent open run; `agave kill --all` stops every
  Colab session.
- Kaggle cannot be cancelled through its API. `agave kill` prints the notebook link; the person stops it there.
- `agave usage` shows the Kaggle weekly quota, Colab unit estimates, and what agave has recorded spending.

## Tokens

Never print, log, commit, or paste a token. The GitHub token file (`~/.kaggle/github_token` unless
`~/.config/agave/config.toml` says otherwise) is read by agave and redacted from remote output. Kaggle and Colab
credentials belong to their CLIs. Uploading or rotating a credential is something the person runs themselves;
`agave init` prints the exact command.

## Verifying a run

A run is verified when `agave run` ended with `OK: exit 0`, `agave outputs` lists the expected files, and the
values inside them look right. Read `outputs/latest/outputs/<file>` rather than trusting the log. When something
fails, `agave logs --full` first; the remote box prints the commit it ran, the pip install, `nvidia-smi`, and the
script's own output in that order.
